newsitem.title: UKRAINE: SOCCER-LOBANOVSKY AIMS TO LEAD DYNAMO TO FORMER GLORY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-LOBANOVSKY AIMS TO LEAD DYNAMO TO FORMER GLORY.

text.p: Valery Lobanovsky, reappointed on Friday as coach to Dynamo Kiev, the club he steered to European success more than 20 years ago, pledged to return the Ukrainian champions to the ranks of Europe's football elite.

"It's an honour to become Dynamo's coach. It also imposes a great responsibility because there are a lot of hopes set on the club's success and they must be realised," Lobanovsky told a news conference.
Dynamo president Hryhory Surkis said Lobanovsky would sign a two-year contract and take up his duties in the new year.
Lobanovsky, the former Soviet national coach, said he would emphasise team plan rather than trying to groom super-star individual players.
"We should not make a team of stars but a star team," he said.
The club tried to lure the 57-year-old Lobanovsky back in 1993 but he was then already contracted to the Kuwaiti national team.

Under his guidance, Dynamo Kiev dominated Soviet soccer two decades ago and won the European Cup Winners' Cup in 1975. They repeated the feat in 1986, the year Lobanovsky became the Soviet team coach.
In all, Dynamo won the Soviet championship 13 times and the Soviet cup nine times.
Lobanovsky will replace current coach Jozhef Sabo, who was given sweeping powers to cut players' pay and bonuses in a "state of emergency" declared after last month's European defeats.
Now playing in the Ukrainian league and with much of Ukraine's best talent preferring to play in Russia or western Europe, Dynamo have struggled.
The team were banned from European soccer for three years after trying to bribe the referee in a Champions' League game against Panathinaikos last year. UEFA later lifted the suspension.
